title: The Unknown value (?) is distinct from null AND zero, and propagates through arithmetic — a discount of ? makes the whole net Unknown
sourceContent:
/* apply-discount.p - net = base - discount, guarding the Unknown value */
DEFINE INPUT  PARAMETER pdBase     AS DECIMAL NO-UNDO.
DEFINE INPUT  PARAMETER pdDiscount AS DECIMAL NO-UNDO.  /* may be ? (Unknown) */
DEFINE OUTPUT PARAMETER pdNet      AS DECIMAL NO-UNDO.

/* If pdDiscount is ? (Unknown), then pdBase - pdDiscount is ? too
   -- the whole net silently becomes Unknown, NOT the base price. */
pdNet = pdBase - pdDiscount.
IF pdNet = ? THEN pdNet = pdBase.   /* explicit Unknown guard */
notes: ABL's Unknown value (?) is a third state distinct from null and from zero, and it propagates: any arithmetic or comparison involving ? yields ?. Here a ? discount makes pdNet Unknown rather than equal to the base, so the explicit `IF pdNet = ?` guard is load-bearing. The Java target must choose a representation for ? (null BigDecimal / Optional / a sentinel) and reproduce the propagation + guard — an openQuestion for the SME.
